rulings.challenge_claim: Two items on one row, distinct defects. First, raised independently on both sides: the comparandum at Jer.49.26 is assigned to the Ammon oracle when its own header bytes place it inside the Damascus unit. Second: MT 50:29 carries two disclosure objects in the single-witness inventory and the row engages only the ketiv/qere note, leaving the paseq unstated, while also tying the ketiv/qere to a named word that a per-verse-count inventory cannot source.
rulings.grounds: Nation attribution is byte-refuted. The lamed header לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק opens MT 49:23 and the next lamed header לְקֵדָ֣ר וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר opens MT 49:28 (byte tier at both); MT 49:27 kindles fire בְּחוֹמַ֣ת דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק (byte tier) and a SAMEKH closes MT 49:27 (tier-3 parashah, single witness). MT 49:26 therefore stands between the Damascus header and the Kedar/Hazor header, inside the Damascus unit. The Ammon header is לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן at MT 49:1 (byte tier) and that unit closes four verses later at 49:6, well before the formula in question. What the row gets right is the match itself: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ stands byte-identical at MT 49:26 and MT 50:30 and at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, verse counts, MT keys), and both named differences hold at byte tier -- אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתָּ֥הּ against אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה, and the closing formula at MT 50:30 lacking the tsevaot carried at MT 49:26. So the shared-texture disclosure survives; only the nation label fails. Second defect confirmed: the single-witness inventory records at MT 50:29 one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg; the row engages the ketiv/qere and never states the paseq, so span-relevant mark symmetry stays open in the row's own middle verse. The word attribution is worse than under-sourced: MT 50:29 carries no unpointed ketiv token anywhere in its verse bytes, and it is one of only two ketiv/qere verses in the book where that is so (2 of the 124 inventoried verses; the other is MT 31:38). Neither the count-only inventory nor the verse bytes can locate that note to a word, so naming one is an unsourced position claim of the same family as a paseq position claim. The remaining grounds hold: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.50.28 reaches byte tier, and the front-seam SAMEKH at MT 50:27 and the closing SAMEKH at MT 50:30 are both inventory-true (tier-3, single witness).
rulings.remedy: Four edits. (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace the Ammon attribution for Jer.49.26 with the Damascus unit, headed at Jer.49.23 and closing at Jer.49.27. Test the cure must pass -- the test that killed the original -- the nation named for a comparandum must be the one whose own lamed header governs the cited verse (Jer.49.23 governs Jer.49.26; the Ammon header at Jer.49.1 closes at Jer.49.6). (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Jer.49.23 and web:Jer.49.27 so the corrected attribution's argued verses are mirrored. (3) boundary_rationale: disclose the paseq at Jer.50.29 count-only, single-witness, with no intra-verse position, alongside the ketiv/qere already named. (4) boundary_rationale: drop the word attribution on the Jer.50.29 ketiv/qere and state the note count only; that verse's bytes carry no ketiv token to splice.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's count for the neum-adonai-YHWH-tsevaot stack is wrong and undigited: it calls the site the second of two such sites when the full stack stands at three verses book-wide, and no scope is stated that would exclude the third.
rulings.grounds: Byte-refuted under the object the row itself names. The stack with tsevaot stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys): MT 2:19 closes נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת, MT 49:5 carries נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת, and MT 50:31 carries נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת (byte tier at all three). Under the wider family that lets tsevaot be optional the count is 4 verses, adding MT 2:22 נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (byte tier), which is a shorter stack and its own object. Either object refutes the digit two, and the row carries no sweep citation naming its swept object and unit -- an exclusivity-shaped count that a tier label on a splice never substitutes for. The rest of the row verifies: הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ זָד֔וֹן and the stack both reach byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.31; the Ammon assignment for Jer.49.5 is correct on the header bytes, unlike the Ammon assignment given to Jer.49.26 in the row closing at Jer.50.30; and both seam marks the row names, the SAMEKH at MT 50:30 and the SAMEKH at MT 50:32, are inventory-true (tier-3, single witness). New finding in the same sentence: the row asserts that its site matches the stack at Jer.49.5 and gives no tier. The two runs are not byte-identical -- MT 50:31 carries merkha, tipcha and etnachta where MT 49:5 carries darga, tevir and tipcha -- so the correspondence holds at accent-stripped and skeleton tiers, not at byte. Against MT 2:19 it holds at skeleton tier only, the retained meteg separating the two at accent-stripped. A recurrence claim carries the tier at which it actually holds.
rulings.remedy: Two edits. (1) device_notes: replace 'the second of two such sites, the other at Jer.49.5 for Ammon' with the swept object named first and its digit -- the neum-adonai-YHWH-tsevaot stack (sweep: 3 verses -- Jer.2.19, Jer.49.5, Jer.50.31) -- and, if the optional-tsevaot family is what is meant, name that as a separate object with its own digit (sweep: 4 verses, adding Jer.2.22). Label the Jer.49.5 correspondence at accent-stripped tier; byte tier fails on the accents. Test the cure must pass -- the test that killed the original -- the digit must survive a re-sweep of the object exactly as named, and every recurrence claim in the field must carry its tier. (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Jer.2.19, and web:Jer.2.22 if the wider family is cited, since those verses would then be argued in prose outside the row's own span.

rulings.challenge_claim: Four distinct defects across two items. Item one: a curly-quoted clause from Jer.50.34 departs from the staged text's own sentence-initial capitalization, breaking verbatim quotation. Item two: the lawsuit-root argument that carries the row's unit_type reasoning is made in transliteration with neither a pointed splice nor a tier and with the root's spread undigited; the paseq inside the row's own span at MT 50:34 is undisclosed while a parashah mark at the front seam is engaged; and a byte-true catchword straddles the row's back seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: All four verify on the bytes. The staged text at web:Jer.50.34 renders the redemption clause as a fresh sentence after the divine-name clause, with a sentence-initial capital; the row's own rendering of that clause opens lower-case, so the curly-quoted run is not verbatim (the field does carry an inline web: ref, so only the verbatim arm fails, not the citation arm). The lawsuit-root argument is carried in transliteration alone in both the rationale and the device note, although the pointed run רִ֥יב יָרִ֖יב אֶת רִיבָ֑ם stands at tokens 6-9 of oshb:Jer.50.34 (byte tier) and is never spliced; no tier is named, the staged extract carries no morphology layer, and the intensive reading behind the rendering is therefore a byte-checkable claim owed pointed bytes. The root's spread is undigited (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys), and the cross-reference to this book's other trial-speech material names no verse, against the verse-anchored cross-reference rule. Mark symmetry: the single-witness inventory records one paseq seg at MT 50:34, inside the row's own span; the row discloses the front-seam SAMEKH at MT 50:32, which is inventory-true, and no disclosure object inside the span it cuts. Cross-seam cohesion: לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closes oshb:Jer.50.34 and וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל stands at oshb:Jer.50.35 (byte tier at both); that construct chain stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys -- Jer.50.34, Jer.50.35, Jer.51.12), two of them either side of this row's own back seam, so undisclosed it argues continuity against the cut. What holds: the onset formula at oshb:Jer.50.33 reaches byte tier with the frame owner named inside the formula itself, and the redemption splice at oshb:Jer.50.34 reaches byte tier. On severity: each item is correctly charged low on its own; the row's combined docket is medium because the cures touch three separate fields and one of them is a seam-pair edit shared with the row opening at Jer.50.35.
rulings.remedy: Five edits, one of them a seam pair. (1) boundary_rationale: restore the sentence-initial capital in the quoted clause from web:Jer.50.34; the cure must pass a verbatim re-check of the whole curly run against the staged text, not of the flagged word alone -- that is the test that killed the original. (2) device_notes: splice the pointed run from oshb:Jer.50.34 beside the transliteration and name its tier; give the root's spread its swept object, unit and digit or drop the spread claim; anchor the cross-reference to this book's other trial-speech material to verses or drop it. (3) boundary_rationale: disclose the paseq at Jer.50.34 count-only, single-witness, with no intra-verse position. (4) SEAM-PAIR CURE, ONE EDIT AT BOTH ENDS: disclose the yoshvei-Bavel construct chain straddling the Jer.50.34 | Jer.50.35 seam, with its swept object, unit, digit and tier, in this row's device_notes and in the device_notes of the row opening at Jer.50.35 -- neither end alone cures it. (5) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.50.35, and web:Jer.51.12 if the chain's digit is cited in prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items converging on the row's front seam. Item one: the row opens a fresh unit at a verse carrying none of this block's licensed internal-cut signals, and its rejected alternative never engages the stronger rival of one continuous declaration from the Jer.50.33 onset. Item two: the pointed wordplay is byte-exact as argued, but a construct chain attested at three verses stands on both sides of the row's own front seam undisclosed, and the sword is described as repeated against a six-item list when two of the items hang off a prepositional chain.
rulings.grounds: The observations are byte-true; the framing overstates what they settle. Byte-true against the row: oshb:Jer.50.35 carries no koh-amar onset, no hoy, no date frame and no vocative, and its only formula token is the mid-verse נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה, which is closure corroboration and not an onset device; its grammar is third-person description governed by a repeated prepositional chain. So none of the internal-cut devices named for this block stands at the onset, and the row's declared scene-shift signal carries the whole warrant. Compounding it, the construct chain stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys -- Jer.50.34, Jer.50.35, Jer.51.12) with לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closing oshb:Jer.50.34 against וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל at oshb:Jer.50.35 (byte tier), a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam and disclosed at neither end. And the row's strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the split at Jer.50.38, never the continuous reading from the Jer.50.33 onset -- confirmed in the field's own text. The list looseness is byte-confirmed too: five sword tokens stand over MT 50:35-50:37 (one at 50:35, two at 50:36, two at 50:37, skeleton tier, MT keys), and the princes and wise men of 50:35 hang off that verse's single sword by the prepositional chain rather than heading their own sword clause; the row's list also drops the two objects that sword actually governs first. What holds and is not contested: the pointing claim is exact at codepoint level -- חֶ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.35 against חֹ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.38 share skeleton and accent and differ in the first vowel alone -- and the anaphora the rejected alternative relies on does run unbroken across 50:35-50:38; mark disclosure inside the span is complete, since no parashah mark, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:35-50:38, so nothing is owed there. Why refine rather than uphold: what the bytes settle is the disclosure gap and the un-engaged rival, not the seam. Internal stanza seams in this Babylon material are held open at a low-confidence posture rather than decided, and a boundary change is a proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work. The corrected finding is an under-warranted and under-disclosed seam carried at too high a confidence, not a demonstrated mis-cut.
rulings.remedy: Four author edits plus one proposal. (1) SEAM-PAIR CURE, ONE EDIT AT BOTH ENDS: device_notes -- disclose the yoshvei-Bavel construct chain straddling the Jer.50.34 | Jer.50.35 seam with its swept object, unit, digit and tier, paired with the same disclosure at the row closing at Jer.50.34. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the Jer.50.38-split rival with the stronger one -- reading the koh-amar-tsevaot declaration opening at Jer.50.33 straight through the litany as one unit -- and answer it on bytes. Test the cure must pass -- the test that killed the original -- the rival engaged must be the strongest available at this seam, not the most easily set aside. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cut the sword sentence to the bytes -- one sword token at Jer.50.35 governing the Chaldeans and, through the prepositional chain, the inhabitants of Babylon, her princes and her wise men; four further sword tokens heading their own clauses at Jer.50.36-Jer.50.37 (sweep: 5 tokens over 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys). (4) confidence: lower to medium_low with a bespoke rationale naming the undisclosed cross-seam chain, matching the held-open posture for internal stanza seams in this material. (5) PROPOSAL ONLY, requiring explicit boss adoption and expressly NOT author work: respan Jer.50.33-Jer.50.38 as one koh-amar-headed unit, absorbing this row into the one before it, as against keeping the cut with the disclosures above. Do not execute without adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The three-verse digit is right but attached to the wrong object: the row calls this site a third occurrence of the Sodom-and-Gomorrah refrain when one of the three counted verses carries no Sodom, no Gomorrah and no overthrow noun.
rulings.grounds: The class blend is byte-confirmed. The clause actually counted, לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם, stands byte-identical at exactly 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, byte tier, verse counts, MT keys -- Jer.49.18, Jer.49.33, Jer.50.40), and the device note scopes that digit correctly. But oshb:Jer.49.33 opens וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד עוֹלָ֑ם (byte tier) and carries none of the three elements the rationale's label names: skeleton sweeps put Sodom at 3 verses and Gomorrah at 3 verses (Jer.23.14, Jer.49.18, Jer.50.40, verse counts, MT keys), while the kaph-prefixed overthrow noun stands at exactly 2 verses -- כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת at oshb:Jer.49.18 and כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת at oshb:Jer.50.40 (byte tier) -- the same skeleton at Jer.20.2, Jer.20.3 and Jer.29.26 being the article-bearing stocks noun, a homograph outside this object. The two overthrow verses are not byte-identical to each other either: Jer.50.40 adds the divine noun and the object markers and closes נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה against אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה at Jer.49.18 (byte tier). So the label fails twice over -- the Sodom-and-Gomorrah element stands at 2 verses in this class, not 3, and the element that does stand at 3 is a different clause. The mislabel is not confined to prose: the row's substrate signal key names the same wrong object, and that field is dependent on the object it declares. Mark symmetry is complete for the span: no parashah mark, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:39-50:40. The onset splice at oshb:Jer.50.39 reaches byte tier. The declared heuristic entry on this row is CONFIRMED a false positive: the flagged word describes the shape of the rejected reading rather than asserting anything exclusive, so no sweep digit is owed beside it. New finding in the closing field: the curly-quoted run for web:Jer.50.40 joins two non-contiguous stretches of the verse with an ellipsis inside one quotation, bridging the intervening neighbor-cities phrase and its speech attribution, so the excerpt is not the contiguous verbatim run it is presented as.
rulings.remedy: Four edits. (1) boundary_rationale: name the swept object before the count -- the closing no-dweller clause (sweep: 3 verses -- Jer.49.18, Jer.49.33, Jer.50.40, byte tier) -- and keep the Sodom-and-Gomorrah overthrow element as its own object with its own digit (sweep: 2 verses -- Jer.49.18, Jer.50.40) if it is cited at all; the two digits stay apart. (2) observed_substrate_signals: replace the refrain key naming the Sodom-Gomorrah formula with a key naming the clause actually counted -- the signal field is dependent on the object swap. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cut the web:Jer.50.40 excerpt to a contiguous verbatim run, or split it into two separately quoted runs each carrying its own inline web: ref, instead of bridging the attribution clause with an ellipsis. (4) Test the cure must pass -- the test that killed the original -- every verse counted under an object must carry that object's own bytes; Jer.49.33 carries neither Sodom nor Gomorrah nor the overthrow noun, and any relabelled count must survive that check.
